11333153_7e2a7ff8.text: Granule cells (GCs) in the dentate gyrus are crucial for transferring information from the entorhinal cortex to the hippocampus proper where they integrate the classical excitatory trisynaptic circuit (McBain, 2008). Although primarily glutamatergic, the axons of GCs, the mossy fibers (MFs), contain GABA, its synthesizing enzyme glutamic acid decarboxylase (Schwarzer et al., 1995)(Sloviter et al., 1996) and the vesicular GABA transporter VIAAT (Zander et al., 2010). In addition, immunogold experiments have demonstrated the presence of both AMPA and GABA A receptors, co-localized on MF terminals in close spatial relation with synaptic vesicles (Bergersen et al., 2003). All these pieces of evidence suggest that MF-cornu ammon (CA3) synapses can use GABA as a neurotransmitter since they posses all the machinery for synthesizing, storing, releasing, and sensing it

11333153_abe1b682.text: electrophysiological experiments from juvenile animals have revealed the presence of mixed GABAergic and glutamatergic monosynaptic currents in CA3 principal cells upon stimulation of GCs in the dentate gyrus (Walker et al., 2001)(Gutiérrez et al., 2003)

11333153_d0620f0a.text: Granule cells are characterized by their peculiar delayed and heterogeneous maturation. Most of them (85%) are generated postnatally.

11333153_c6f84ad2.text: Granule cells are characterized by their peculiar delayed and heterogeneous maturation, with most of them (85%) being generated postnatally (Pedroni et al., 2014).

11333153_3bc75fe5.text: immediately after birth, GCs exhibit a clear GABAergic phenotype. Only later they integrate the classical glutamatergic trisynaptic hippocampal circuit
